entities.name: The Translation Movement (Bayt al-Hikma)
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The systematic translation of Greek philosophical, scientific, and medical texts into Arabic, centered at the Bayt al-Hikma (House of Wisdom) in Abbasid Baghdad (c. 750–1000 CE). Under caliphs al-Mansur, Harun al-Rashid, and especially al-Ma'mun (r. 813–833), teams of translators — including the great Hunayn ibn Ishaq — rendered virtually the entire Greek philosophical and scientific corpus (Plato, Aristotle, Euclid, Ptolemy, Galen, Hippocrates) into Arabic, often via Syriac intermediaries.

This movement preserved Greek knowledge that might otherwise have been lost, created the Arabic scientific vocabulary, and catalyzed the Islamic Golden Age of original scholarship in mathematics, astronomy, medicine, optics, and philosophy.
